subject: POC onboarding journey, exit criteria and owner matrix — BorealTech
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@borealtech.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC onboarding journey, exit criteria and owner matrix — BorealTech

Hi Anna — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight onboarding journey so we can get to an actionable POC that proves value for your search/retrieval flow. Please skim and confirm anything missing.

Top-level objective
- Validate that Redwood inference can reduce user search latency and improve relevance on BorealTech's product search use case while staying within cost targets.

Mandatory (gate) success criteria
- 95th percentile latency for search-serving generation < 200ms at 50 req/s sustained
- Precision@10 lift >= 10% vs current baseline on the provided eval slice
- End-to-end cost per served request < $0.03 (tokens + infra)
- Secure onboarding: masked PII, audit logs enabled, and SSO + RBAC for your users

Aspirational (stretch) criteria
- Reranking throughput at 200 qps with average latency < 250ms
- Content-aware caching achieves 30% token reduction for repeat queries

Proposed timeline & milestones (draft)
- Week 0 (Kickoff) — May 3: account & infra prep, data ingest checklist, SSO test account
- Week 1 — May 10: model + quantization recommendation, baseline ingestion & initial validation
- Week 2-3 — May 17–28: run live trial on a subset (shadow traffic) + weekly check-ins
- Week 5 — Jun 4: final readout, decision gate and go/no-go recommendation

Owners (initial)
- Redwood engineering lead: Camila Reyes — infra, model tuning, SSO enablement
- Redwood Customer Success: Marissa Cole — cadence, success metrics, stakeholder alignment
- BorealTech PM: Anna Li — data access, acceptance decisions
- BorealTech Eng: Tom Rivera — test harness + deployment verification

Next actions for BorealTech (please confirm)
- Confirm the attendees for kickoff and preferred week of May 3
- Provide the redacted sample eval set (CSV/Parquet) and a small quota of production-like requests for baseline measurement
- Share procurement timeline for MSA / PO so we can align environment provisioning (if needed)

Attachments: boreal_poc_proposed_timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet), poc_playbook_v1.md (doc), poc_success_metrics.xlsx (template)

If this looks good I will circulate an updated timeline with calendar invites and a short runbook for the first 48 hours post-kickoff.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Li <anna.li@borealtech.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@borealtech.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC onboarding journey, exit criteria and owner matrix — BorealTech

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the recap and the clear gates. A few quick clarifications:

1) Data/masking: Our security team requires that any sample data used for evaluation be masked for customer identifiers. We can provide a masking script; can Redwood consume masked CSV/Parquet?
2) Mandatory vs aspirational: I like that split. Can you mark the document so that procurement and executive sponsors see which items are non-negotiable?
3) Procurement: I expect our legal/procurement to ask for a short-form SOW and an MSA. Can your team surface a draft SOW and a standard MSA for review? Our procurement timeline is ~2–3 weeks once we share the procurement contact.

Kickoff week: May 3 works for us today. Tentative attendees: me, Tom (Eng), plus Security (TBD).

On the latency numbers — the 95th <200ms requirement is aggressive but aligns with our goals. Curious what you expect for sample traffic volume for the initial baseline runs (how many requests and what distribution).

Thanks,
Anna
Head of Product — BorealTech

On Fri, Apr 24, 2027 at 9:15 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Anna — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight onboarding journey...
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@borealtech.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC onboarding journey, exit criteria and owner matrix — BorealTech

Thanks Anna — answers inline and an updated, slightly more prescriptive plan attached.

Data/masking: Yes — Redwood can consume masked CSV/Parquet. We recommend you include an ID mapping file (kept offline) so we can run labeled evaluations without PII.

Procurement & docs: I'll attach a short SOW template and our standard MSA redline. Marissa will loop in solutions if you want an SOW tailored to the traffic profile.

Sample traffic for baseline runs:
- Initial baseline: 5k–10k requests across the eval slice (spread across common, long-tail queries)
- Shadow traffic: 1–2 hours at expected peak rate (if feasible) during Week 2 to validate stable latency under load

Revised mandatory vs aspirational — marked in attached poc_success_metrics.xlsx. Highlights:
- Mandatory: 95th <200ms @ 50 req/s sustained, Precision@10 uplift >= 10%, cost per request < $0.03, SSO/audit enabled
- Aspirational: reranking throughput 200 qps, caching savings 30%

Cadence & owners (finalized)
- Kickoff: Mon May 3, 10:00 AM PT (1 hour) — invite will be sent; deliverables: access matrix, baseline data drop, success metrics agreed
- Weekly check-ins: Tuesdays 9:00 AM PT (30 minutes) — Camila (Redwood eng) leads technical sync; Marissa leads success metrics tracking
- Engineering tasks: data ingest & masking verification (Camila) — due May 7
- Model tuning window: May 10–28 (Camila)
- Shadow/traffic validation: week of May 17 (joint)
- Final readout: Jun 4, 11:00 AM PT — Marissa to present results & recommendation
- Decision gate: Jun 6 (internal BorealTech decision window)

Risk mitigations
- If procurement delays infra access, we will start with a synthetic/obfuscated data run to validate infra and model parity (no PII needed).
- If observed latency > target during shadow, fallback plan: enable lightweight quantized variant + increase cache TTLs to meet 95th percentile targets while we iterate on model size.

Attachments: updated_poc_timeline.xlsx, poc_success_metrics.xlsx, redwood_sow_template.docx
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/12345
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfG...

I'll send calendar invites for kickoff and the recurring Tuesday check-ins. Anything else to add to the agenda for kickoff?

-Vivek
